column1: # CAP-3U Currency return matrix - the declared expectation per target and case.
# `must_pass`  a PASS has been MEASURED on the toolchain that leg builds with;
# `observe`    the case is run and recorded, and fails nothing. It is the
#              verdict for a case whose behaviour is a known upstream defect,
#              and for a case nobody has yet measured on the leg's own
#              compiler. Turning one into `must_pass` is a deliberate act.
# Windows is `must_pass` throughout because the 2026-09-08 pin move measured
# 5/5 on FPC 3.2.2 x86_64-win64 - the exact toolchain `fpc.lock` pins for that
# leg - against 0/5 at the previous pin unpatched.
# Linux is `observe` for a reason worth writing down: the same 5 cases were
# measured 1/5 at this pin and 0/5 at the previous one, so four of them are a
# known upstream defect on SysV x64 rather than anything this repository can
# fix; and the one that passes was measured under FPC 3.2.3, while the hosted
# leg builds with Ubuntu's 3.2.2. Declaring `must_pass` from a different
# compiler would be a prediction, not a measurement.
# Both macOS rows are `observe` because they have never been measured at all.
# macos-x86_64 shares ABISYSVX64 with Linux and macos-arm64 does not - AAPCS64
# is a different ABI with its own CallMethod - so neither may be inferred from
# the other, and the first hosted run of this gate is what will say.
